staleness_rationale: w_stale = 1 / (1 + staleness). A gentle, transparent discount â€” a client that is 1 round behind keeps half its sample-count weight, 2 rounds behind a third, etc. Chosen as the simplest non-trivial staleness-aware rule, before seeing any result.

no_correction.rationale: Control condition: clients sync/skip exactly as their real simulated availability dictates (so staleness genuinely varies round to round), but aggregation ignores it entirely â€” every client's update is weighted by sample count alone, identical to Phase 6's rule. Isolates whether staleness-blind aggregation under real, non-trivial staleness degrades results relative to Phase 6's own (synchronous, staleness-free) numbers.

linear_decay.rationale: w_stale = 1 / (1 + staleness). A gentle, transparent discount â€” a client that is 1 round behind keeps half its sample-count weight, 2 rounds behind a third, etc. Chosen as the simplest non-trivial staleness-aware rule, before seeing any result.

exponential_decay.rationale: w_stale = 0.5 ** staleness. A more aggressive discount than linear_decay for the same staleness value (1 round behind -> 0.5x instead of 0.5x already matches linear at staleness=1, but diverges sharply after: 2 rounds behind -> 0.25x vs. linear's 0.33x). decay_rate=0.5 chosen as a round, interpretable default, not tuned against any result.

config.notes: Phase 9 is NOT reinforcement learning: no reward signal, no policy network, no learned parameters â€” see src/federated/staleness.py for the exact deterministic formulas. All 8 clients participate (train and submit an update) in every round for every config; what differs is (a) which global-model state a client actually trains against, driven by its real Phase 4 `availability_probability`, identically across all three configs (same `participation_seed`), and (b) how much a stale update's contribution is discounted before aggregation. This is the first phase to make Phase 4's simulated availability field actually gate round-to-round participation â€” Phase 8's `resource` signal reads the same underlying simulated fields but only as a static weighting input, never as a participation gate.
